title: Phrasing in practice
goal: Whole phrases as single strokes: worked examples, what it saves, and how to try the grammar today.

blocks.x: Keys in steno order: left bank (starter), vowels and star, then the right bank. When there are no vowels or star, a `-` marks the start of the right bank, as in {{I am}} [[SWR-B]].

*there* takes *be*, *have been* and the modals only, not the other verbs, and no bare *do*: [[=there is|STHR-B]], [[=there was|STHREB]], [[=there would be|STHROEB]], [[=there must have been|STHRAUFB]].
What it takes from today's dictionary

37 of the 3,758 grammar strokes are held by something today: 19 merged two-word phrases and 18 short forms, extras and backups of rare words. The generator will place the grammar first so the displaced words settle on their next outline. In the prototype no word is left without an outline.

Measured by `tools/phrasing_prototype.py` over today's dictionary with today's merged phrases taken first. By tier, starter plus auxiliary alone saves 0.6%; adding *be*, *have* and *have been* takes it to 1.4%; the 20 verbs to 2.1%. Five verbs (*say*, *see*, *know*, *think*, *go*) are 46% of the verbs' share. The novels are third-person past narration, so everyday first- and second-person present typing has more of these pairs per word and this undercounts it.

cargo run --release -- build
python3 tools/phrasing_prototype.py         # writes out/grammar-trial/
cp out/grammar-trial/02-lyk-*.json ~/.config/keymux/steno/lyk/

The trial folder is the whole `02-lyk-*` set with the displaced entries removed and the grammar added as `02-lyk-grammar.json`. `lyk deploy` puts the normal dictionary back (it removes any `02-lyk-` file it did not write).

items: Questions: *do you*, *are you*, *can I* (the starter after the auxiliary).
More verbs, chosen by measured gain.
